paragraphs: The paper studies how to estimate a treatment’s causal effect when an unobserved factor influences both treatment and outcome. It considers linear structural causal models with access to just one proxy variable. Such a proxy provides indirect information about the hidden confounder, but existing approaches can require restrictive assumptions or additional proxies.

The proposed method uses cross moments: quantities that summarize how treatment, outcome, and proxy values vary together through products of their values. The authors show that, in their setting, a non-Gaussian latent confounder allows the causal effect to be identified through simple arithmetic on these quantities. This relaxes the equal-effect condition underlying the difference-in-differences comparison discussed in the paper.

The distributional condition matters. The authors also prove that identification is impossible when the observed treatment, outcome, and proxy are jointly Gaussian. Experiments on synthetic and real data support the approach’s effectiveness. Together, the results explain both an opportunity for estimation with one proxy and a setting where observational information cannot identify the effect.
neurips-2023-a-cross-moment-approach-for.tldr: Cross moments can identify causal effects with one proxy in the studied linear models when the latent confounder is non-Gaussian.

paragraphs: An agent with limited vision must decide both how to act and what to observe. These decisions influence each other: the selected view affects the next action, while actions change which observations are useful. The paper studies this coupled problem in partially observable environments, separating task actions into a motor policy and observation choices into a sensory policy.

Its framework, SUGARL, represents the two policies separately but learns them together. A learned reward module supplies an intrinsic sensorimotor reward that encourages the sensory policy to select observations useful for inferring the agent’s own motor action. This gives observation selection a training signal connected to what the agent does.

Experiments report effectiveness across multiple levels of observability and show that the framework can work with existing reinforcement learning algorithms. The learned sensory policies also exhibit effective active vision strategies. These findings support using the relationship between seeing and acting to coordinate the policies, rather than treating observation selection as an unrelated prediction task.
neurips-2023-active-vision-reinforcement.tldr: SUGARL jointly trains action and observation policies using a learned reward that connects visual choices to the agent’s actions.

paragraphs: When a data distribution changes over time, past observations may no longer describe the situation a model must handle now. This paper studies learning from independent observations collected over the last T time steps, with performance measured against the distribution at the current step. The challenge is that the amount of distribution drift is unknown.

The authors develop an algorithm that adapts directly to the observed data without explicitly estimating the drift. Its analysis compares it with a learner that already knows the magnitude of the drift. The adaptive method achieves almost the same error, showing that advance knowledge of this quantity is not required to approach that reference level of performance.

The method can also guarantee lower learning error than an approach based on overly loose drift bounds. This makes adaptation useful beyond simply removing an input requirement: it can avoid the cost of pessimistic assumptions about change. The paper demonstrates the general technique in binary classification and linear regression, retaining independent observations as a stated premise.
neurips-2023-an-adaptive-algorithm-for-l.tldr: A data-adaptive learning algorithm handles unknown distribution drift with error close to a learner that knows the drift magnitude.

paragraphs: A generative model can produce convincing examples while missing substantial parts of a dataset’s variety. This paper evaluates diversity through modes, the distinct components of a multimodal distribution. Its motivation is that existing quality and diversity scores do not have a clear correspondence with how many such components a model captures.

The authors propose using Rényi Kernel Entropy, or RKE, as an information-theoretic diversity score. They show that it can return the number of modes for a mixture of sub-Gaussian components, giving the score a mathematical interpretation in that setting. They also establish bounds on estimation error from limited samples, suggesting rapid convergence toward the underlying distribution’s score.

The paper applies RKE to widely used generative models on standard image datasets. In these evaluations, newer training approaches improve mode-based diversity relative to earlier architectures but still fall short of the diversity in real data. The resulting rankings therefore concern diversity as measured by RKE, connecting an interpretable statistical quantity to an empirical comparison of generated samples.
neurips-2023-an-information-theoretic-ev.tldr: The paper uses Rényi Kernel Entropy to evaluate mode coverage and finds that tested generative models still miss some real-data diversity.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary segmentation asks a model to identify image regions belonging to categories introduced at inference time. Category names can be a weak interface: they may be incomplete, ambiguous, unfamiliar to a pretrained model, or difficult for a user to formulate. AttrSeg addresses this problem by representing categories through multiple attribute descriptions.

The method first decomposes a class name into descriptions that supply complementary semantic context. It uses large language models to construct attributes for common categories and manual annotation for human-invented categories. It then aggregates the attributes into a global description that helps distinguish the target category from other objects. A hierarchical architecture and clustering module combine information at multiple levels.

Segmentation is obtained by comparing the aggregated attribute representation with image embeddings. To evaluate this approach, the authors add attribute annotations to three datasets and conduct experiments and ablation studies, reporting superior performance. The contribution is a richer way to specify visual categories, supported by results showing the value of decomposing and recombining their descriptions.
neurips-2023-attrseg-open-vocabulary-sem.tldr: AttrSeg improves open-vocabulary segmentation by decomposing categories into attribute descriptions and aggregating them into visual classifiers.

paragraphs: Formal verification of deep reinforcement learning systems can become expensive and overly conservative. The paper attributes a major part of this difficulty to overestimation introduced during training and when converting a neural decision model into a form suitable for verification. Such overestimation makes the verification calculation less tightly reflect the system being analyzed.

The proposed approach reverses the usual order: it first encodes a neural network as an equivalent collection of linear control policies that can be verified efficiently and tightly, then optimizes them through reinforcement learning. Piece-wise linear decision neural networks, or PLDNNs, provide the model structure for this approach. They are compatible with most existing deep reinforcement learning training algorithms.

Experiments report task performance comparable to conventional neural networks, alongside verification speedups of up to 438 times and substantially reduced overestimation. The authors also verify a 12-dimensional system with up to seven times deeper computation steps. These results support designing verifiability into the policy representation before training, with the reported gains applying to the evaluated systems.
neurips-2023-boosting-verification-of-de.tldr: PLDNNs structure reinforcement learning policies for verification before training, enabling tighter checks and reported speedups of up to 438 times.

paragraphs: Transferring learned behaviors to a new task can be easier than learning everything again. The Option Keyboard pursues this by adaptively combining existing behaviors using successor features and generalized policy improvement. Its practical burden is that the state features and task encodings must be designed by hand for each environment.

The Successor Features Keyboard removes that hand-design requirement by learning the representations needed for transfer. Its central learning algorithm, the Categorical Successor Feature Approximator, estimates successor features while jointly discovering state features and task encodings. This ties representation learning to the requirements of the mechanism that will later combine behaviors.

The authors demonstrate transfer in a challenging three-dimensional environment with all necessary representations discovered. Among the successor-feature approximation methods they compare, only their algorithm learns representations compatible with successor features and generalized policy improvement at this scale. Their full system also transfers fastest to long-horizon tasks among the tested transfer baselines. The findings show that discovering suitable representations can make behavior combination work in this more demanding setting.
neurips-2023-combining-behaviors-with-th.tldr: The Successor Features Keyboard learns the representations needed to combine existing behaviors and transfer quickly to tested long-horizon tasks.

paragraphs: Image-to-image translation must change an image in a desired way while maintaining consistency with its source. This remains challenging when using pretrained diffusion models without paired examples of the desired transformation. CycleNet introduces cycle consistency into diffusion-based image manipulation as a way to regularize those changes.

The paper evaluates the method across transformations at different levels of detail, including changes to scenes and objects. It also contributes a multidomain image-to-image dataset focused on changes in objects’ physical states. That addition broadens the evaluation beyond scene or object translation to transformations involving the state of an object.

The empirical studies report better translation consistency and image quality. They also show high-quality outputs for out-of-domain distributions after a simple change to the text prompt. CycleNet remains robust in the reported setting with roughly 2,000 training examples and can be trained using one GPU. These findings support cycle consistency as a practical constraint for text-guided manipulation, with evidence spanning several kinds of unpaired image translation.
neurips-2023-cyclenet-rethinking-cycle-c.tldr: CycleNet adds cycle consistency to diffusion-based image editing and reports improved translation quality with limited training data.

paragraphs: Translating EEG signals into text often depends on markers that divide brain activity into word-level segments. Those markers can be difficult to obtain during inference, and the order of eye fixations may differ from word order. DeWave introduces a discrete representation of EEG activity to reduce these obstacles in open-vocabulary translation.

A quantized variational encoder converts EEG waves into discrete codes that are aligned with pretrained language models. Text–EEG contrastive training helps address ordering mismatches, while the shared discrete representation reduces interference from differences between individuals’ EEG signals. The representation therefore serves both as an interface to language modeling and as a way to handle variability in the input.

On the ZuCo dataset, DeWave reports 41.35 BLEU-1 and 33.71 Rouge-F, exceeding the stated previous baseline scores. The paper also reports translation of entire EEG periods without word-order markers, achieving 20.5 BLEU-1 and 29.5 Rouge-1. This latter result demonstrates a distinct, marker-free capability, with its own reported performance rather than the scores from the other evaluation.
neurips-2023-dewave-discrete-encoding-of.tldr: DeWave connects discrete EEG codes to language models and demonstrates text translation without word-level order markers on ZuCo.

paragraphs: Learning sentence representations that express shared meaning across languages usually benefits from parallel corpora: collections of corresponding text in different languages. Such data can be scarce or unevenly available. EMMA-X aims to learn cross-lingual representations with the help of abundant multilingual text that does not come in parallel pairs.

The method combines sentence representation learning with an additional task that predicts semantic relationships between sentences. It places a sentence encoder and a semantic relation classifier within an expectation-maximization-like framework. Both components approximate the semantic relationship of a sentence pair, and their predictions provide supervision for each other until convergence. This makes the relation task part of the representation-learning process.

The authors evaluate EMMA-X on xrete, a newly introduced benchmark containing 12 cross-lingual tasks that depend on sentence-level representations, and report state-of-the-art performance. A geometric analysis using three requirements also favors its representation space over advanced comparison models. The evidence supports the usefulness of mutual supervision for learning shared meaning from multilingual nonparallel data.
neurips-2023-emma-x-an-em-like-multiling.tldr: EMMA-X uses mutually supervising sentence and semantic-relation models to learn cross-lingual representations from multilingual nonparallel data.

paragraphs: Inverse protein folding seeks amino acid sequences compatible with a specified protein backbone. Many sequences can correspond to the same backbone, so the task involves representing multiple plausible answers as well as recovering a viable sequence. The paper explores diffusion modeling as a way to address this one-to-many relationship.

Its graph denoising diffusion model uses the given backbone to guide generation of amino acid residue types. It models their joint distribution using the nodes’ physicochemical properties and local environments. The forward diffusion process also uses amino acid replacement matrices to incorporate biological prior knowledge about residues and their spatial and sequential neighbors, reducing the space the generative process must explore.

The authors report state-of-the-art sequence recovery relative to the popular baselines they evaluate. They also describe strong potential for generating diverse sequences for a fixed backbone. These are related but distinct findings: the recovery result establishes performance on that measured objective, while the diversity finding supports the broader motivation for modeling multiple possible sequence solutions.
neurips-2023-graph-denoising-diffusion-f.tldr: A backbone-guided graph diffusion model improves reported sequence recovery and shows potential for generating diverse compatible protein sequences.

paragraphs: Predicting several people’s movements requires understanding more than their individual motion. People respond to each other, objects, and the layout of their surroundings. Someone planning to use a coffee machine, for example, may wait when another person occupies it. Humans in Kitchens provides data for studying these intertwined influences.

The dataset contains more than 7.3 hours of recordings across four kitchen scenes, with as many as 16 people present simultaneously. It includes over four million annotated human poses represented through a parametric three-dimensional body model. Scene geometry and each person’s activities are annotated per frame, alongside changing scene geometry and objects such as chairs and cupboards.

These annotations connect movement to the surrounding people and physical environment, providing information needed to investigate context-aware forecasting. The paper also introduces two evaluation protocols covering short-term and long-term prediction. Its contribution is therefore both a detailed record of multiperson activity and a framework for evaluating forecasts over different time horizons, rather than a reported improvement from a particular forecasting model.
neurips-2023-humans-in-kitchens-a-datase.tldr: Humans in Kitchens supplies detailed multiperson motion and scene annotations, plus protocols for short- and long-term forecasting.

paragraphs: In a heterophilous graph, connected nodes tend to have different labels. Graph neural networks designed for this setting often use repeated computations involving nonlocal relationships. These operations can be costly on large graphs and difficult to organize into minibatches, limiting the scale at which the models can be trained.

LD2 separates graph propagation from model training and constructs expressive node embeddings beforehand. Moving this work outside training simplifies the learning process and enables lightweight minibatch updates. The authors’ theoretical analysis establishes optimal training time complexity and a training memory footprint that does not depend on the scale of the graph.

Experiments on large heterophilous graphs report speed improvements of up to 15 times, efficient memory use, and predictive performance comparable to or better than the evaluated baselines. The results connect the architectural separation to practical scalability: training can use precomputed graph information without repeatedly performing the expensive graph operations that burden existing approaches. The stated complexity result specifically concerns training.
neurips-2023-ld2-scalable-heterophilous-.tldr: LD2 precomputes graph embeddings to enable efficient minibatch training on heterophilous graphs, with reported speedups of up to 15 times.

paragraphs: A single-index model generates its output by projecting a high-dimensional input onto one unknown direction and applying a nonlinear function. Despite this compact structure, learning the hidden direction provides a useful test of whether gradient methods can discover features beyond a linear model. Much existing theory studies this problem with Gaussian inputs.

Gaussian distributions have stability and spherical symmetry properties that make the analysis tractable. In that setting, earlier results connect sample complexity to an information exponent associated with the nonlinear link function. This paper asks how much of the learning picture can extend beyond Gaussian data, where those helpful distributional properties may fail.

The authors focus on a planted setting in which the nonlinear link function is known. Under assumptions described as mild, they prove that stochastic gradient descent recovers the unknown direction with constant probability in the high-dimensional regime. The result broadens the established recovery theory beyond Gaussian inputs while retaining both the known-link premise and the qualified probability of success.
neurips-2023-on-single-index-models-beyo.tldr: The paper proves qualified recovery guarantees for stochastic gradient descent on single-index models beyond Gaussian data when the link function is known.

paragraphs: Clustering quality can depend on how compact each group is or how well different groups are separated. This paper studies the latter, less understood optimization problem. It focuses on minimum spacing, the closest distance between points in different groups, and minimum spanning tree spacing, which measures separation through the cost of connecting all groups.

The authors develop algorithms with provable guarantees for maximizing these criteria. They address both unrestricted clustering and a constrained version requiring every group to contain a minimum number of points. This requirement is motivated by single-linkage clustering: although it optimizes both criteria without constraints, it can produce many tiny groups.

The minimum-size condition therefore brings a practical grouping requirement into a separation-based objective. Alongside the theoretical results, an empirical study on ten real datasets provides evidence that the proposed methods work well in practice. The contribution combines guarantees about the optimization problem with observed usefulness, addressing separation without accepting arbitrarily small clusters as an unavoidable outcome.
neurips-2023-optimization-of-inter-group.tldr: The paper develops clustering algorithms with provable guarantees for separation objectives, including settings with minimum cluster sizes.

paragraphs: Reconstruction attacks can reveal private information by recovering recognizable images from a model. Privacy assessments often use image-quality measures such as PSNR and SSIM to compare reconstructions with originals. This paper asks whether those measures agree with what people can actually recognize, which is central to the privacy interpretation of a reconstructed image.

The authors study five datasets, four attack methods, and multiple classification models. Several human annotators judge whether each reconstruction is recognizable. The existing hand-crafted measures correlate only weakly with these judgments and often disagree with one another, showing that overall image similarity can be an unreliable proxy for the assessed privacy leakage.

The proposed alternative, SemSim, learns semantic similarity from the human annotations. Its triplet training uses an original image, a recognizable reconstruction, and an unrecognizable reconstruction. SemSim correlates substantially better with human judgments, and this relationship generalizes in the reported evaluations to unseen datasets, models, and attacks. The findings support evaluating recognizable semantic information more directly when assessing reconstruction-based privacy risk.
neurips-2023-privacy-assessment-on-recon.tldr: Human-trained SemSim tracks recognizable information in reconstructed images more closely than the hand-crafted metrics evaluated in the paper.

paragraphs: QLoRA reduces the memory needed to adapt large language models by keeping the pretrained model frozen in four-bit form and training low-rank adapters through it. The paper reports enough memory savings to finetune a 65-billion-parameter model on one 48 GB GPU while preserving the task performance of full 16-bit finetuning.

Three components support this efficiency. NormalFloat provides a four-bit representation that is information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights. Double quantization compresses the constants used in quantization, and paged optimizers manage memory spikes. The authors study more than 1,000 finetuned models across eight instruction datasets, multiple architectures, and several model sizes.

Their Guanaco model family reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT’s performance level on the Vicuna benchmark, with 24 hours of single-GPU finetuning. The paper also finds that small, high-quality datasets can yield leading results. However, its evaluation analysis questions the reliability of current chatbot benchmarks and documents Guanaco failures relative to ChatGPT, so the benchmark percentage should retain its specific evaluation context.
neurips-2023-qlora-efficient-finetuning-.tldr: QLoRA combines frozen four-bit models with trainable low-rank adapters to substantially reduce finetuning memory while preserving reported task performance.

paragraphs: Large recommender systems commonly retrieve items by embedding a query and candidate items into a shared space, then searching for nearby candidates. This paper proposes a different retrieval mechanism: a model generates the identifier of the item it predicts the user will interact with next. Retrieval thus becomes a sequence-generation task.

The method assigns each item a Semantic ID composed of a tuple of meaningful codewords. A Transformer sequence-to-sequence model receives the Semantic IDs of items in a user’s session and learns to predict the next item’s ID one part at a time. The identifiers supply semantic structure to the prediction task, rather than functioning only as arbitrary item labels.

Experiments report significant improvements over current state-of-the-art models across several datasets. The authors also find improved retrieval for items without previous interaction history when Semantic IDs are incorporated into the model. That result supports the claim that meaningful identifiers improve generalization, alongside the broader finding that generating identifiers can be an effective recommendation retrieval strategy.
neurips-2023-recommender-systems-with-ge.tldr: A recommender generates meaningful item identifiers directly, improving reported retrieval performance and generalization to items without interaction history.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning improves representations by drawing similar examples together and separating dissimilar ones. In medical image segmentation with few labels, selecting genuinely dissimilar examples is difficult. Supposedly negative examples may contain similar anatomy, and rare classes can be hard to distinguish. The paper connects these problems to misclassification and model collapse.

ARCO approaches this issue through variance-reduced estimation and stratified group theory. Its sampling techniques are designed to improve contrastive learning for pixel- and voxel-level segmentation, particularly when labels are extremely limited. The authors provide a theoretical proof of universal variance reduction for the proposed sampling techniques, giving the sampling design a statistical basis.

The method is evaluated on eight benchmarks: five medical segmentation datasets spanning two and three dimensions, plus three semantic segmentation datasets. Across the tested label settings, it consistently outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods. Adding the sampling techniques to contrastive learning frameworks also produces significant gains. These results support improving how training examples are sampled as a useful intervention in learning dense representations from scarce labels.
neurips-2023-rethinking-semi-supervised-.tldr: ARCO uses variance-reducing sampling to improve semi-supervised segmentation, with theoretical support and gains across eight evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge into models with limited capacity, but many proposed improvements are designed and judged on small datasets. This paper argues that such evaluations can underestimate ordinary, or vanilla, distillation. Its central question is how the relative value of elaborate distillation methods changes when data and training conditions become more substantial.

The authors find that larger datasets and stronger data augmentation directly reduce the performance gap between vanilla distillation and more carefully engineered variants. They also compare approaches under stronger training strategies and different model capacities. These investigations make the training setting part of the comparison, rather than assuming conclusions from small-scale experiments carry over unchanged.

Using vanilla distillation, the paper reports ImageNet top-1 accuracies of 83.1% for ResNet-50, 84.3% for ViT-S, and 85.0% for ConvNeXtV2-T, described as state-of-the-art results. The findings establish vanilla distillation as a strong option in the studied large-scale settings and motivate evaluating proposed improvements under conditions that reflect their intended use.
neurips-2023-revisit-the-power-of-vanill.tldr: Larger datasets and stronger augmentation narrow the gap between vanilla knowledge distillation and specialized variants in the paper’s evaluations.

paragraphs: Urban event ranking aims to identify the locations at greatest future risk of events such as crimes or traffic accidents. When resources are limited, the order of locations matters directly. Predicting an event count or risk score for every location does not necessarily produce a good ranking, especially when neighboring places have similar features.

SpatialRank combines ranking optimization with a model of spatial and temporal dependence. Adaptive graph convolution layers learn changing relationships between locations. A hybrid loss uses surrogate objectives for NDCG and includes a spatial component to improve comparisons among nearby locations. Importance sampling with spatial filtering makes this loss practical to evaluate during training.

The paper evaluates SpatialRank on three real-world datasets and reports effective identification of the highest-risk locations. Its NDCG improvement over state-of-the-art methods reaches up to 12.7%. These results support directly optimizing ranking quality while accounting for dependencies between places, addressing the mismatch between independent-item ranking methods and urban data whose locations influence or resemble one another.
neurips-2023-spatialrank-urban-event-ran.tldr: SpatialRank combines learned spatial-temporal dependencies with ranking-focused training to identify high-risk urban locations.

paragraphs: This paper addresses two obstacles in training large vision-language models: computation cost and sudden training instability. For speed, it introduces SwitchBack, a linear layer supporting eight-bit integer training. On a one-billion-parameter CLIP ViT-Huge model, it reports a 13–25% speedup while remaining within 0.1 percentage points of bfloat16 training performance.

The authors also examine float8 training through simulation. SwitchBack works in that setting, while standard methods can also succeed when initialization and training discourage large feature magnitudes. They achieve this using layer-scale initialized to zero. This finding connects low-precision training behavior to the magnitude of internal features.

For stability, the paper finds that loss spikes consistently follow underestimation of squared gradients by AdamW’s second-moment estimator, appearing one to eight iterations later. It recommends a hybrid of AdamW and Adafactor that avoids spikes in the evaluated CLIP ViT-Huge training and outperforms gradient clipping at the tested scales. Together, the results provide separate interventions for faster arithmetic and more stable optimization.
neurips-2023-stable-and-low-precision-tr.tldr: SwitchBack accelerates low-precision vision-language training, while an AdamW–Adafactor hybrid avoids loss spikes in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Standard denoising diffusion models use a Markovian structure that makes extensions beyond Gaussian or discrete distributions difficult. This paper introduces a star-shaped diffusion process that avoids needing to specify transition probabilities or compute posteriors. The change expands the distributions that can be used to construct diffusion models.

The authors establish a duality between star-shaped processes and particular Markovian diffusions for distributions in the exponential family. They derive efficient training and sampling algorithms, and show that the Gaussian version is equivalent to a standard diffusion model. The same framework also provides a construction recipe for Beta, von Mises–Fisher, Dirichlet, Wishart, and other distributions.

These alternatives may be especially useful when data occupies a constrained manifold, where distribution choice can reflect that structure. Evaluations across different settings find competitive performance, including a Beta model with image-generation results comparable to a Gaussian diffusion model. The contribution is therefore both a mathematical reformulation and evidence that the broader distribution choices can remain practically effective.
neurips-2023-star-shaped-denoising-diffu.tldr: Star-shaped diffusion broadens the choice of noise distributions while retaining efficient algorithms and equivalence to standard diffusion in the Gaussian case.

paragraphs: A tester-learner combines a check on the data distribution with a learning algorithm whose error is guaranteed whenever that check accepts. This paper develops such a system for halfspaces, or linear decision boundaries. Its tester works across a broad class of structured distributions instead of targeting just one particular distribution.

The fully polynomial-time method guarantees error O(opt) + epsilon on any accepted labeled distribution, where opt represents the best achievable halfspace error. It accepts whenever the input marginal satisfies a Poincaré inequality. This class contains strongly log-concave distributions; inclusion of all log-concave distributions follows if the KLS conjecture holds.

When label noise is known to satisfy the Massart condition, the result strengthens to opt + epsilon and accepts every log-concave distribution without requiring KLS. The tests use sum-of-squares optimization to check hypercontractivity, drawing on certificates available for Poincaré distributions. The contribution ties broad distributional acceptance to explicit learning guarantees while distinguishing the general result from the stronger, noise-specific case.
neurips-2023-tester-learners-for-halfspa.tldr: A polynomial-time tester-learner guarantees halfspace learning error across a broad distribution class, with stronger results under Massart noise.

paragraphs: A classifier cascade adjusts prediction cost by deciding whether each input needs another model’s attention. A common rule stops when the current classifier is confident and otherwise passes the input onward. This can work well, but the current model’s confidence does not explicitly describe how useful the next model will be.

The paper characterizes the optimal deferral rule theoretically and uses that result to identify settings where confidence-based decisions may perform poorly. The key issue is that deciding whether to continue depends on the structure of the cascade, including downstream model errors. Confidence in the current answer can leave out information relevant to that decision.

The authors then study post-hoc deferral mechanisms and demonstrate significant improvements in three settings: downstream specialists that work well only on some inputs, noisy labels, and shifts between training and test distributions. These findings clarify when simple confidence rules deserve closer scrutiny. They support alternative deferral strategies in the studied conditions without implying that confidence-based cascades generally fail.
neurips-2023-when-does-confidence-based-.tldr: The paper characterizes optimal cascade deferral and shows when post-hoc alternatives can outperform rules based only on current-model confidence.
